transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Dubois, thank you for meeting with me. Your daughter, thank you for being here as well. I need to discuss something that happened during your surgery yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am still feeling very tired. Why are we talking now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. To be direct, a mistake was made during the procedure. A small metal clip, which is used to seal blood vessels, was placed on the wrong structure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I mean that the clip went where it wasn't supposed to go. We call it a misplaced clip. Because it was in the wrong spot, we had to perform an additional step in the surgery to remove it and fix the area. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Non... je ne comprends pas. Why would this happen? You are surgeons.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is shocking to hear. I am very sorry that this happened. The responsibility lies with me and the surgical team. We did not place that clip correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I trusted you. I put my life in your hands and you are telling me you just... you made a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is deeply upsetting to feel that trust has been broken. I can see that you feel let down by us, and you have every right to be angry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like a fool. To lie there and think everything is fine while you are making errors. C'est ridicule.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It isn't ridiculous to feel that way. You were in a vulnerable position and we failed to meet the standard of care you deserved. I truly apologize for the distress this is causing you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And this additional procedure... did it cause more damage?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a fair question. We caught the error while you were still under anesthesia, so we were able to correct it immediately. Because we fixed it right then, there is no long-term damage to your organs. Do you have any questions about the clip itself or how we found it?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if I am okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are stable, and the correction was successful. But I realize that knowing you are physically okay doesn't take away the feeling that this shouldn't have happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly. I am a man of my word, I expect the same from my doctors. I feel... insulted.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. You value precision and integrity, and we didn't provide that yesterday. I am truly sorry for wounding your confidence in us.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, first, I will make sure your records reflect exactly what happened. Then, I'll check your incision site again in about an hour to make sure everything is healing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be back tomorrow morning to see how you're feeling before we discuss the discharge date.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You say you are sorry, but how do I know the next person won't do the same thing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that worry. I can't undo what happened, but I can tell you that we are reporting this to our quality board today. We will review the tapes of the surgery to see where the lapse occurred so we can prevent it from happening to another patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Just tell me when I can go home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you're exhausted and you just want this to be over. I'm sorry, I have to get to another patient quickly, but I'll be back shortly to check your dressing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are rushing now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're right. I apologize. I will be back in one hour. Is there anything else you need from me right this second?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. Just go.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language ('I have to get to another patient quickly') near the end of the encounter.

E.justification: The error (misplaced clip) is named in the second turn, lay language is used, and comprehension is checked twice ('Does that make sense so far?' and 'Do you have any questions...').

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language and explicitly takes responsibility ('The responsibility lies with me and the surgical team') without deflection.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('shocking', 'let down', 'angry', 'vulnerable', 'insulted') and references the patient's values of precision and integrity.

T.justification: The resident provides specific next steps and timelines and addresses prevention, but fails to name a role for the patient in the plan.
